newsitem.title: UK: London bullion fixes firmer after finding support.
newsitem.headline: London bullion fixes firmer after finding support.

text.p: Precious metal prices were under some pressure on Thursday but found support after New York opened trying to recoup Wednesday's losses.
Earlier Europe had come into line with overnight moves in New York and Asia.
"The markets are pretty quiet but they don't look that great," one dealer said, emphasising the platinum group metals (PGMs) looked particularly vulnerable.
Gold was fixed at $321.00 versus $318.95 at the morning fixing, reviving after support was found on the Comex December futures contract in New York.
Bullion was likely to remain under pressure following forecasts that the dollar would hold around 1.88 to the mark in the foreseeable future and close to recent highs against yen, dealers said.
Even so shortly after the fixing bullion was standing at $321.50/$322.00 when the December Comex contract was indicated at $325.50, up $3.00.
But some dealers believed a probe of the 12-year low just under $314.00 was likely.
Another bear issue was the risk of producer hedging on any uptick. "There is a lot of hedging still to be done out there," one dealer said.
The expiry of options on the New York's Comex gold and silver futures markets on Friday was likely to hold prices around current levels until next week, dealers said.
Platinum and palladium both bounced modestly after being sharly lower at the opening following long liquidation on Nymex and a limit-down move on Tokyo's Tocom futures exchange.
"The Japanese liquidation wiped out all the gains of the past three days and put the market under renewed pressure," a dealer said.
The Japanese selling followed the widening of daily limits on Tocom after six limit up sessions and a sell-off on Nymex which was said to include selling by a hedge fund
Russia's few deliveries to Japan and sporadic parcels being sold in Europe had taken some of the heat out of the markets' illiquidity.
Even so, one-month lease rates for platinum and palladium were still being quoted at a historically colossal 20 percent and 80 percent respectively.
Platinum was indicated at $432.00/$435.00 down just $2.50 and off an opening low of $419.00/$422.00.
Palladium was at $219.00/$222.00 down $9.00 and a dollar above its opening.
Silver also recoved early losses to be a cent firmer at $4.37/$4.39 but dealers said the downside was still favoured after an attempt to filla chart gap at $4.50/$4.55 was abandonded on Tuesday.
